study: Does large-kernel perception help small grayscale image classification
supporting_paper: An Image is Worth More Than 16x16 Patches: Exploring Transformers on Individual Pixels (ICLR 2025)
learning_rate_rule: Evaluate both rates for every variant on original validation data. Select the FULL variant's highest validation accuracy at its loss-selected checkpoint; tie break validation loss then smaller rate. Use this ONE common rate for every primary variant, seed and condition. Other variants' optimal pilot rates are reported only as validation sensitivity diagnostics.

budget_diagnostic.role: Secondary single-seed training-budget diagnostic, not a reproduction of the ImageNet recipe

primary_claim: Large-kernel perception improves classification relative to no perception depthwise convolution or a 3x3 perception kernel within the same adapted LSNet framework.
spatial_extension: Does the full-versus-control accuracy gap change after the same fixed pixel permutation used in Assignment 1? This affects several spatial modules, not only LKP.
checkpoint_selection: Validation loss must improve by more than min_delta. Test metrics never select settings, checkpoints or stopping.
pilot_reuse: Reuse each seed-42 original pilot at the selected common rate as that primary run. Do not count reuse as an independent fit.
test_disclosure: The official Fashion-MNIST test set was inspected during Assignment 1. It is a reused benchmark, not a newly blind holdout. All Assignment 2 checkpoints and evaluation identities are frozen before loading its test arrays.

timing.notes: Same allocated GPU, FP32, eval mode, unfused, resident tensors, CUDA synchronization; compare with existing Assignment 1 checkpoints under this same protocol.

bootstrap.notes: Pair models and average fitted seeds first. Interval is conditional test-group uncertainty, not all training uncertainty.

publication: Private files only. Do not publish, upload to a public repository, email, or fabricate contributions.
